novelty_basis: An elementary narrow-pipe property of byte-level e-transformations. Quasigroup hash designs submitted to the SHA-3 competition used huge quasigroups in wide-pipe constructions (Edon-R, orders 2^256-2^512, https://ehash.isec.tugraz.at/uploads/7/74/Edon.pdf; NaSHA, https://eprint.iacr.org/2008/519), which avoids it; two searches found no explicit statement of the bound for byte-level e-transformation hashes.
proof_check: Lean 4 + Mathlib for the factorisation of the tail through one state (eT_append, eT_tail_factors) and injectivity (eT_injective); the counting consequences by written proof (proofs/paper/C18.md Theorem 3); the bound is attained exactly (256 values) in 100 families of 4096 keys (EXP-C18-05) and explains the 32,624 full collisions of EXP-C18-03 exactly
statement:
The last k outputs of an e-transformation are a bijective function of the state before them and the last k
inputs. Hence a hash outputting the last 8 bytes after p forward e-transformations takes at most 256^p values on
messages sharing their last 7 bytes, and with a final reversed e-transformation it takes at most 256 values on
messages sharing their first 7 bytes, for every p and every quasigroup of order 256.
title: The tail-information bound: an e-transformation tail carries one byte of state
